top_choice_rationale: Optical-lattice quantum simulation is the one shortlisted field where nobody disputes maturity: the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and single-site quantum gas microscopy turned the Hubbard model into a tunable laboratory system, reproduced by many groups over twenty years. A mixed citation naming the realisation (Bloch, Greiner) and the theoretical proposal (Zoller) says what actually happened in the field and absorbs the Cirac-Zoller overlap with the theory-only case. The experiment-only trio (P005) is my second choice, the Katori-Ye clock (P001) has the cleanest credit but narrower reach, the Higgs prize (P002) has the strongest science but an unresolved attribution rule for three names across two collaborations, and the magic-angle graphene prize (P003) is eight years old with an unsettled pairing mechanism and omitted experimentalists. A prize in any of these is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Profile-based conflict only for circuit QED (not a proposal on this slate): I work in superconducting circuits, direct WACQT and have Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson. No specific connection to the laureates in P001-P005 is apparent; WACQT's superconducting-qubit platform competes with the cold-atom and ion approaches of Zoller and Cirac, disclosed for transparency.
